why_this_rate: The unit's own output ends between sixteen and eighteen kilohertz, measured: thirty-two decibels over silence at sixteen, sixteen at seventeen, nothing at eighteen. A chain running at thirty-two kilohertz ends exactly there. The rate is part of the candidate rather than a constant, so a reading above the half-rate is dropped by name instead of being answered with a number the model never said.

map.why: Two states and the boundary is between 0 and 1: one value of the byte selects one corner and the other 127 select the other. The figure is the half point of the deviation, which is where this model's corner parameter is defined.
The byte answers over a window of twenty-five values centred on 64 and sticks at both ends. Read at every value between 48 and 80: 52 and below return the same cut and 76 and above the same boost.

reached_by.why: The same blend with a second shelf stored at full cut for the other side of the byte rather than the boost inverted. A shelf is two rows a corner state, so storing the cut costs little and the argument that ruled this out for a peak -- eighty rows doubled -- does not reach it here.

map.why: The named third octaves between the printed ends, indexed by the byte's top four bits. Read off the page and the era rather than off these takes: the fitted positions this model used to carry sit up to a sixth of an octave below the table at the bottom of the range, which is a curve fitted over a peak two octaves wide being pulled towards its longer flank. At the narrowest width the unit's peak stands in the band the table names. One entry of the sixteen is not the series: the third sits at 279.1 Hz where the named third octave is 315.0, on both mid addresses of this type and on the mid section of two combination types. The frequency class publishes that figure as a readout beside its claim and holds the entry open, and this candidate carries it. Fifteen entries here could have come out wrong and one could not, which is why the candidate without it is ranked beside this one rather than replaced by it.

The five figures the page prints, halved. Scored against every band profile of this type whose swept address is a mid width byte: the printed figures give seven times the residual and lean on two of the three records that carry a feature, and the halved list leans on none. Nothing in it was fitted.
The byte answers over a window of twenty-five values centred on 64 and sticks at both ends. Read at every value between 48 and 80: 52 and below return the same cut and 76 and above the same boost.

reached_by.why: One section stored at the top of the printed range and blended against the dry path. In coefficients the denominator never moves and the numerator is three multiply-accumulates between two stored rows, which is what a control processor of the era would rather spend on a parameter change than a sine and a square root. The cut is the same section with its numerator and denominator exchanged, which is what the cookbook's peaking section does and costs nothing to store.

map.why: Two states, as the low corner. Both figures are lower bounds: the deviation was still climbing where the band set ended, so the half point they are read from is the half of a peak the bands did not reach.

map.why: Every setting of the byte, as the level of the whole take against the level at 127. Settings whose take sat within three decibels of the chain's own silence are left out: what those return is the room and the converter, not the byte.

the_second_mid_is_not_measured_separatel: M2's centre and width were asked at three settings each and returned M1's figures to the printed digit, so the two mids share one map here. Three settings is what asking whether they answer alike costs; it is not a second reading of the curve.
what_varies: Whether the two shelves are built at the gain their bytes name or stored once at full scale and blended against the dry path. Both mid sections are blended in every candidate here, which is what their own class closed on, and every table, corner, window and level is the one the type's claim closed on.
rendered_through: The equaliser's low shelf, because its gain byte is the only shelf gain in the archive swept at every setting between the ends of its window. The high shelf's records are scored too and separate nothing: they hold three settings and two of them are the window's ends, where all three candidates are one section.
